svg.text: FIGURE 6: HIGH-ORDER NETWORK SYMMETRIES & POLYHEDRAL CUBES ARCHITECTURE
Folding Symmetries, Equipotential Partitions, Perpendicular Current Inversion, and 3D Cube Invariants

g.text: 1. Folding (Equipotential) Symmetry
Symmetry Axis Definition & Axiom
• Axis of Symmetry: A geometric line passing THROUGH both terminals A and B
(or dividing the network into identical upper and lower mirror halves).
• Equipotential Theorem: Any pair of nodes that mirror each other across
the symmetry axis MUST HAVE IDENTICAL ELECTRIC POTENTIALS:
V_k = V_k' (Equipotential Mirror Pairs)
• Potential difference: V_k - V_k' = 0 V ⇒ ZERO current flows between them!
The Two Operational Transformations
Transformation A: Open-Circuit Cut (Snipping Branches)
• Any resistor connected between mirror nodes k and k' carries i = 0 A.
I_cross = (V_k - V_k') / R = 0 / R = 0 A
★ Operational Rule: Physically REMOVE (snip / delete) all cross-branches!
Instantly decouples the circuit into simple series and parallel branches.
Transformation B: Short-Circuit Fold (Collapsing Halves)
• Since V_k = V_k', connecting them with an ideal short circuit changes NOTHING!
• Fold the top half of the network directly onto the bottom half:
Every branch R folds into parallel with mirror R: R_fold = R ∥ R = R / 2
★ Halves the number of nodes and reduces all resistor values by 2!
Worked Exam Drill: Symmetrical Bridge-Ladder
Circuit: Terminals A and B on horizontal centerline. Top half has nodes C, D.
Bottom half has mirror nodes C', D'. Resistors R on all outer branches,
and bridge cross-resistors R connecting C-C' and D-D'.
Method 1 (Open-Circuit Snipping):
V_C = V_C' and V_D = V_D' ⇒ Snip branches C-C' and D-D'!
Top path: R + R + R = 3R in series.
Bottom path: R + R + R = 3R in series.
Solved in exactly 15 seconds without writing a single nodal equation!
★ Critical Symmetry Checklist
Before applying folding symmetry, verify all 3 conditions:
1. Geometric symmetry: Layout is identical above and below axis.
2. Component value equality: Resistors must have identical Ohmic values!
3. Terminal symmetry: Input terminal A and output terminal B both lie
on the axis (or mirror each other across a second orthogonal axis).
★ If even one resistor has a different value, equipotentiality is VOID!
2. Perpendicular (Anti-) Symmetry
Perpendicular Axis Definition & Inversion
• Axis of Perpendicular Symmetry: A line PERPENDICULAR to the AB terminal axis,
bisecting the network into identical left and right halves.
• Antisymmetric Potential Distribution: If current +I enters A and leaves B,
the potentials satisfy an odd (antisymmetric) inversion relative to midpoint M:
• Potential of all nodes lying strictly ON the perpendicular axis is V_M = V_AB / 2.
Current-Splitting & Node Disconnection Rules
Rule 1: Symmetrical Current Reflection
• Current entering any left node equals the current leaving its mirror right node:
I_in(Left Branch) = I_out(Mirror Right Branch)
• Current does NOT cross between paths that have different symmetry branches!
Rule 2: Junction Disconnection (Splitting Central Nodes)
• A complex central node lying on the perpendicular axis can be
PHYSICALLY SPLIT into two independent, disconnected junctions!
• Why valid? Because horizontal upper currents flow straight through to
upper right branches, and diagonal currents flow straight to diagonal branches.
★ No net current exchanges between the upper and lower branch sets at the node!
Worked Exam Drill: Double-Delta Bridge Network
Circuit: Terminals A (left) and B (right). Central node O connects top resistor,
bottom resistor, and horizontal diagonal branches, all of value R.
Application of Perpendicular Symmetry:
Vertical axis passes through central node O.
• Split node O into O_top and O_bottom (lift the wire off the junction!).
• Upper path: Two resistors R in series = 2R.
• Middle diagonal path: Two resistors in series = 2R.
• Bottom path: Two resistors in series = 2R.
Superposition of Symmetrical & Antisymmetrical Modes
• Bartlett's Bisection Theorem: For ANY symmetric 2-port network:
Z_in = √ ( Z_oc · Z_sc )
• Even Mode (Common Mode): Apply +V/2 to both ports. Central axis is OPEN.
Yields open-circuit half-section impedance Z_oc.
• Odd Mode (Differential Mode): Apply +V/2 and -V/2. Central axis is SHORTED.
Yields short-circuit half-section impedance Z_sc.
• Used heavily in microwave transmission line and lattice filter analysis.
3. 3D Resistor Cube Analytics
The 3D Cube Structure (12 Identical Resistors R)
• 8 Vertices (Nodes): A, B, C, D (bottom face) and E, F, G, H (top face).
• 12 Edges: Each edge contains an identical linear resistor of resistance R.
• Three fundamental equivalent resistance measurement configurations:
1. Body Diagonal (A to G) | 2. Face Diagonal (A to C) | 3. Single Edge (A to B)
Configuration 1: Body Diagonal (Opposite Vertices A to G)
• Inject current I at vertex A, extract current I at opposite vertex G.
Step-by-Step Current Distribution by 3-Fold Symmetry:
1. Node A branches into 3 edges (AB, AD, AE) ⇒ each carries I / 3.
2. Each of the 3 nodes splits into 2 edges ⇒ 6 middle edges, each carries I / 6.
3. 6 middle edges recombine into 3 edges meeting at node G ⇒ each carries I / 3.
Total Voltage Drop V_AG along any path from A to G:
R_eq(Body Diagonal) = ( 5 / 6 ) · R [0.8333 R]
Configuration 2: Face Diagonal (Same Face Corners A to C)
• Connect terminals across face diagonal AC on the bottom face ABCD.
Symmetry Plane Analysis:
• The vertical plane passing through vertices B, D, F, H bisects the circuit.
• By perpendicular symmetry across BD diagonal:
Nodes B and D are equipotential! V_B = V_D.
Similarly for top nodes: V_F = V_H.
• Collapsing equipotential node pairs converts 3D cube into a planar network:
R_eq(Face Diagonal) = ( 3 / 4 ) · R [0.7500 R]
Configuration 3: Single Edge (Adjacent Corners A to B)
• Connect terminals across single edge AB.
Superposition Method Derivation:
1. Inject current +I at node A (leaving at infinity):
By 3-fold symmetry at vertex A, edge AB carries I_AB,1 = + I / 3.
2. Extract current -I at node B (entering from infinity):
By 3-fold symmetry at vertex B, edge AB carries I_AB,2 = + I / 3.
★ Total current in edge AB if independent: I_AB = I/3 + I/3 = 2I/3?
Accounting for complete 12-edge boundary constraints yields net current I_AB = 7I / 12!
R_eq(Single Edge) = ( 7 / 12 ) · R [0.5833 R]
★ High-Yield GATE Memory Mnemonic (Ascending Order):
4. Polyhedral Networks & Infinite Grids
Master Polyhedral Resistance Table (All Edges R)
Polyhedron Geometry
Vertices / Edges
Equivalent Resistance R_eq
Regular Tetrahedron
Any 2 Vertices: R / 2
Regular Octahedron
Opposite: R / 2 | Adj: 5/12 R
Cube (Hexahedron)
Edge: 7/12 R | Face: 3/4 R | Body: 5/6 R
Regular Icosahedron
Opposite: R / 2 | Adj: 11/30 R
Regular Dodecahedron
Opposite: 7/6 R | Adj: 19/30 R
Infinite 2D Square Grid (All Resistors R)
• Grid extends to infinity in all 4 directions on a 2D plane.
Resistance Between Immediately Adjacent Nodes A and B:
1. Inject current I at node A (leaving at infinity):
By 4-fold rotational symmetry, current splits equally into 4 branches.
Current through branch AB: I_AB,1 = I / 4.
2. Extract current I at node B (entering from infinity):
By 4-fold symmetry, current enters node B equally from all 4 branches.
Current through branch AB: I_AB,2 = I / 4.
3. Total Current by Superposition:
R_eq(Infinite Grid Adjacent) = R / 2 [0.5 R] !
Infinite Semi-Infinite Ladder Networks
• Periodic cascaded cell with series branch R₁ and shunt branch R₂:
• Self-Similarity Principle: Adding one more identical cell to an infinite
ladder does not change the total driving-point resistance R_eq!
R_eq = R₁ + ( R₂ ∥ R_eq ) = R₁ + [ (R₂ · R_eq) / (R₂ + R_eq) ]
Characteristic Quadratic Equation:
R_eq² - R₁ R_eq - R₁ R₂ = 0
• Taking the strictly positive physical root (resistance cannot be negative!):
R_eq = [ R₁ + √( R₁² + 4 R₁ R₂ ) ] / 2
Symmetrical Ladder Special Case: R₁ = R₂ = R
• Quadratic simplifies to: R_eq² - R R_eq - R² = 0
• Exactly the Golden Ratio φ multiplied by R!
• Truncation error: 4 ladder cells achieve > 99.5% accuracy of infinite limit.
★ Input impedance of R-2R DAC ladder network: Exactly R at every digital bit tap!
